items: Crucial Removal Provision: Although a State Information Commissioner is appointed by the Governor, they can only be removed by the President of India after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
2019 Amendment Impact: Salary and tenure are no longer pegged to Election Commissioners; they are now entirely determined by the Central Government.
Selection Committee Composition: The Prime Minister (or Chief Minister at state level) heads the committee, accompanied by the Leader of Opposition and a nominated Cabinet Minister.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Both the Central Information Commission (CIC) and State Information Commission (SIC) were constituted under the provisions of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005.
The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners at the Central level are appointed by the President of India based on the recommendations of a three-member committee.

State Chief Information Commissioners and State Information Commissioners are appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee comprising the Chief Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly, and a State Cabinet Minister.
Following the RTI (Amendment) Act 2019, the tenure, salaries, and service conditions of both Central and State Information Commissioners are prescribed by the Central Government.
Neither Central nor State Information Commissioners are eligible for reappointment to the same office upon completion of their term.
